reference: The runnable contract expectations use Bash's documented type -t and help builtins plus the declared prlimit synopsis and help text in the pinned loadable contract. GNU util-linux prlimit and Linux RLIMIT/prlimit semantics are the intended independent oracle for deferred operation coverage; no operation oracle was invoked here.
coverage: Bash identifies prlimit as a builtin with type -t.
Bash detailed help exposes the documented query, set, range, output-format, and command-mode synopsis.
Bash brief help exposes the documented command summary.
Deferred: resource queries and text/raw/JSON formatting.
Deferred: limit parsing, set behavior, and validation in a disposable target.
Deferred: selected-PID behavior and permission/missing-target errors.
Deferred: child command inheritance, exit propagation, and exec failure behavior.
exclusions: No prlimit operation was executed: query, set, selected-PID, or command mode.
No GNU util-linux operation comparison was run; operation cases remain deferred under the task's safety instruction.
The suite does not test effects on the host shell or any host process.

cases.purpose: Confirm through Bash metadata that the candidate registers prlimit as a builtin.
Check Bash help against the declared documented query, command, range, and output forms without invoking prlimit itself.
cases.script:
doc=$(help prlimit)
[[ $doc == *'prlimit(8) subset over prlimit(2).'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *'prlimit --pid PID -r RES SOFT[:HARD]'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *'prlimit --nofile=SOFT[:HARD] COMMAND [ARG...]'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *'Ranges: SOFT, SOFT:HARD, SOFT: (keep hard), :HARD (keep soft), unlimited.'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *'Output: default text lines, --raw tab-delimited lines, or --json objects.'* ]] || exit 1
printf '%s\n' 'pid query/set, command mode, ranges, and output formats documented'
cases.stdout: pid query/set, command mode, ranges, and output formats documented

cases.purpose: Bash help -s publishes the registered invocation synopsis, including PID selection and command mode; help -d is the description.
cases.script:
summary=$(help -s prlimit)
[[ $summary == *'--pid PID'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $summary == *'--nofile=LIMIT COMMAND'* ]] || exit 1
printf '%s\n' 'brief command summary documented'

cases.purpose: Cover current-process and selected-PID reads, including default text, raw columns, JSON, resource selection, and unlimited-value rendering.
cases.reason: The task explicitly excludes prlimit operations from execution. A future fixture needs a disposable Linux VM or controlled syscall mock with a worker initialized to fixed RLIMIT values; compare the builtin's selected-resource, all-resource, raw, and JSON output to GNU util-linux prlimit or an independent encoder, including unlimited values.

cases.purpose: Cover numeric and unlimited limits, SOFT:HARD and partial-range forms, soft-greater-than-hard rejection, invalid values, and preservation of unspecified sides.
cases.reason: The task explicitly excludes limit-setting operations. A future fixture needs a disposable process whose limits can be initialized, changed, read back, and discarded, or a controlled prlimit64 syscall mock. It must verify only that expendable target's limits change and that malformed or invalid requests do not alter them.

cases.purpose: Cover explicit --pid selection, invalid and nonexistent PIDs, and permission errors without touching unrelated processes.
cases.reason: Meaningful cross-PID checks require controlled process identities and target lifetimes. A future fixture needs same-UID and restricted disposable workers in a private PID namespace or a syscall mock, so GNU util-linux and the builtin see stable targets and EPERM/ESRCH cases without referencing host PIDs.

cases.purpose: Cover command-mode limit inheritance, parent-state preservation, child exit/signal propagation, and exec failure status.
cases.reason: Command mode forks, changes a child's resource limit, and execs a command. A future fixture needs a disposable VM or controlled syscall/process mock plus a private reporting helper to verify inherited limits, parent preservation, and status mapping without involving host commands or processes.
